object_description: apparently monolithic volume stacked on a recessed glazed base
design_condition: the large form is placed on the outer edge of the perimeter and splits the site into an upper entrance and playground level and a lower play and sports level

positive: Atmospheric tension between the spatial density of the body and the openness of the outdoor area
The basic spatial-functional concept appears clear and significant
Special uses in the base create a certain public character
Small-scale room clusters organised above create an introverted learning landscape
The lower large rooms are lit through the glazed ground floor
negative: The two site levels create a dichotomy unfavourably accentuated by the striking height difference
The entrance area with its large staircase appears oversized and inappropriate for the location
The lower area is a wild juxtaposition of playing fields without spatial qualities
Narrow green strips with few trees degenerate into mere residual areas
No coherent, overarching open space concept was developed
The two classroom floors are equivalent in plan but differ in lighting and use quality
The desired small-scale resolution proves a disadvantage, especially for the middle floor
Etched glass slat cladding appears superimposed and makes the school barely visible from outside
Lack of other public uses on the ground floor reinforces the invisibility
The future extension thickens the building greatly and obscures the simple urban principle
Structurally the two stacked room typologies do not work together
